scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported Antarctica record covers 1945 to 1994. It is a continent, not a state, people or a claim of uniform sovereignty; region classification makes that distinction visible without changing the source geometry.
The card does not settle competing priority claims for first sighting or first landing, or invent a date for the beginning of Antarctic human history.

Hut descriptions and conservation reports were read as published text. The embedded audio tour and original artefacts were not personally examined. The mutton’s exact expedition attribution and the interpretation of dog stretchers remain qualified.
Cape Evans expedition dates are distinguished from the 2022 exposure and conservation report date. Newly visible objects are not all newly discovered or unrecorded.

The card reports the 1985 ozone discovery and historical international response. It omits the institutional page’s simplified forecast of complete recovery and does not imply that the Montreal Protocol immediately banned every listed chemical worldwide.

The ice-core description uses the 2023 research abstract and short summary; it is not a claimed review of every method or underlying dataset. No claim that Dome C remains the oldest available core is made.

The 2020 food and water accounts refer to Australian stations, not every national program. Macquarie Island infrastructure is not assigned to the Antarctic continent. Variable staffing counts are omitted.
The BAS women’s history is institution-specific. The source’s 1976 spelling inconsistency and broad first-woman claims are not reproduced.
Treaty and protocol summaries were checked against the Secretariat. Territorial claims are preserved, not universally recognized or abolished; the protocol has no automatic 2048 expiry.
Independent historical review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending.
